newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said five percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, 14 percent in poor, 33 percent fair, 41 percent good and seven percent excellent.
The report reflects the impact of a cold snap that has damaged winter wheat crops in Kansas, Texas and Oklahoma.

In its report on conditions for the week ended April 27, USDA said 45 percent of the Kansas wheat crop rated very poor to fair versus 60 percent last week. In Texas, 76 percent of the crop was in very poor to fair condition versus 68 percent last week. And in Oklahoma, 71 percent of the wheat rated very poor to fair versus 58 percent last week.

The USDA report also said that 16 percent of the winter wheat crop had headed, mainly in the Southeast, southern plains and California, compared to 12 percent one year ago and the five-year average of 15 percent.
Five percent of the spring wheat crop was planted compared with nine percent the same period a year ago, and the five-year average of 23 percent, USDA said.
USDA said 18 percent of the corn crop was planted versus 21 percent the same period a year ago, and 15 percent average.
The department also reported 21 percent of the cotton crop was planted, compared with 19 percent in the same period in 1996 and the five-year average of 24 percent.
Nineteen percent of the sorghum crop was planted, compared to 20 percent one year ago and the five-year average of 22 percent.
USDA also said 14 percent of the U.S. rice crop had emerged verus 20 percent one year ago and the five-year average of 24 percent. -- Washington Commodities Desk (202) 898-8394
